chunks: From him, from Usman ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was on a journey, riding upon his she-camel. When he dismounted, he prostrated with five prostrations. So when he mounted, they said, 'O Messenger of Allah! We saw you doing something you had not done before.' He said, 'Yes. Jibraeel (peace be upon him) came to me and gave me glad tidings from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. So I prostrated to Allah in gratitude, one prostration for each glad tidings.'
ai.seo_question: Why did the Prophet Muhammad perform five prostrations during his journey?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi’s chapter on Gratefulness, this hadith highlights the Prophet’s spontaneous gratitude (shukr) through prostration upon receiving divine glad tidings via Jibraeel. It underscores the Shia emphasis on expressing thankfulness not just verbally, but through physical acts of worship, establishing a precedent for the virtue of prostrating in gratitude for specific blessings.
